description: The body carriers: the nude parts every character wears under its garments, and the folders a garment's own body pieces come from. Ours: the client's paper doll is Python, so no Carbon source states these. parts: each nude part, drawn while nothing covers or replaces it, with the dependant categories whose dependants it names as its own carriers (the torso's sleeves). garmentDependants: the dependant categories whose models are body pieces a garment can ask for (sleeves, collar, hood); each model there is a carrier a worn garment shows. cutMaskClip: which nude carrier areas the composed cut mask clips (the clip parameter set to 1): an area holding the mask resource whose influence parameter is above the threshold. At 0 (legs_nude) the shader's alpha is the composed bake's, which clipping would cut away; a garment's own body piece is never clipped. meshCopy: when a shown garment model carries its own copy of a nude carrier's mesh (the same mesh name, and at least share of its bind-pose vertices on the carrier mesh's, positions compared at 1/positionScale metres), the carrier's mesh is hidden and the garment's draws in its place. Chosen from the measured female corpus: robeaf01's cloth TorsoShape 0.000; the reshaped LegsShape of nine bottom families 0.209 (pantsprtf01) to 0.809 (pantsmf01); 0.1 sits between them. shells: whether a nude carrier's cut-mask shells draw (a mesh whose every area is transparent with the cutMaskClip influence above its threshold: torso_nude's Torso5Shape, BridgeShape and Torso4Shape). Not drawn (operator, 27 October 2026: nothing seen so far needs them): the neck shell's top sits 1.8 mm under the head, a visible seam; the nape patch draws an unpainted atlas corner; the shells poke through tight tops. backingCutout: every carrier's opaque and decal areas whose cutout colour parameter has a weight above alpha are set to alpha, so the backing areas draw the composite instead of darkening towards their cutout colour (the male torso's backing has no separate shell). Edit freely: the engine reads this file as data.
